newsitem.title: CHINA: Nantong Container says to delay B share offer.
newsitem.headline: Nantong Container says to delay B share offer.

text.p: China's Nantong Smooth Sail Container Co Ltd has decided to postpone a plan to offer B shares because of falling company profits, company officials said on Thursday.
"The issue plan has been put off," a company official said by telephone. "Because current market conditions are not good, we will have to take a wait-and-see attitude."
The container maker, based in Nantong in eastern Jiangsu province, is among 33 domestic enterprises approved this week to list B shares by the Securities Commission under the State Council.
The company's B share offer had been exclusively handled by its parent company -- China International Marine Container Co Ltd, which is based in Shenzhen and listed on the Shenzhen stock market.
"Work on the B share issue has been temporarily suspended, we have no plan for any issue in 1997 or 1998," an official of China International Marine Containers said.
Marine Containers holds a majority 51.8 percent stake in Nantong Smooth Sail Containers and would have a final say on a B share offer and listing, he said.
"The delay was partly because of the company performance and also because of the scale of the company, its scale is not big enough," the official said.
Nantong Containers had planned to issue B shares to raise funds for future production expansion, officials said.
"We have not killed off the plan, we are still working on it," the Nantong Container official said. "We just want to delay it for some time, to wait for our business to recover.
"We could issue shares now, but they (investors) would not be happy," he said.
Gross output value of Nantong Container reached $118 million in 1996 and it earned about $100 million from exports, he said.
The company remained profitable in 1996, but profits declined because of weak demand for containers and excess production in the industry, he gave no further details.
